newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 7.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The bulk of revenues for 1997 will come from the combination of the cutbacks on tax exemptions - estimated at bringing in an annual revenue of 120 billion drachmas - and the non-indexation of the tax scale, according to reports. --The European Commission makes its formal warning to the Greek government that it will no longer ignore Greece's growing deficits and says a cut off of Cohesion Funds could be the consequence.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis's meeting with his economic team yesterday made the final touches to the 1997 budget, which will be discussed at party meetings and the Cabinet next week.The major topics of discussion were the bill on cutting tax breaks, while incomes policy, taxation of state titles, derivatives and real estate still need work.

--Inflation unrelenting at 8.3 percent year-on-year. The latest figures indicate that the government will be hard-pressed to achieve inflation below 8.0 percent by the end of the year and that 1997's forecast target of 5.5 percent will need serious
--The national economy ministry has decided to make its presence felt in the capital market, establishing a working group to oversee monitoring bodies in the Athens Stock Exchange.

--Yesterday's meeting between Simitis and Papandoniou decided to abolish tax breaks on tutorial and lawyers' fees and donations but to keep tax relief for hospital and medical care for those earning less than 20 million drachmas, and on first home loans and home rentals.
--There will be tighter criteria in the development law for subsidies following an "investment boom". This year, subsidies passed the 220 billion drachma mark.
--The Commission has not yet ruled out sending Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies to Athens to discuss the report the Commission will prepare on the economy by the end of the year.
--There is optimisim for a continuing drop in inflation towards the end of the year as October figures show a slight drop from 8.5 to 8.3 percent.

--State titles to carry 7.5 percent tax on interest while tax relief for medical care and insurance will stay. --October a productive month for state revenues, according to first reports from the finance ministry. Revenues for October had a growth rate of around 15 percent, above the forecast budget target of 13.6.

--The Commission has stressed that it is not prepared to wait for Greece and that bold measures are needed immediately. The price for ignoring this warning will be the cut off of Cohesion Fund monies.

--It is still uncertain whether the economic measures to be included in the budget will be discussed by party and government bodies, other than the Cabinet. Although Papandoniou said the dimensions of 1997's budget have been decided there are three outstanding issues that the government has yet to deal with - the real estate tax, whether taxation of state titles will be retroactive and the improvement of objective tax criteria.

--Federation of Greek Industries President Jason Stratos says Commission's warning of cutting Cohesion Fund monies should not be blown out of proportion and that the entire issue is routine. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
